title: Sharks Have Bitten the Cables That Carry the Internet

scenes.text: Sharks have bitten the cables that carry the internet.
About 99 percent of international internet traffic travels through cables on the seabed.
Shark bites were reported as early as the late 1980s.
Scientists suspect electric fields from the cables make them seem like prey.
So Google wrapped its trans-Pacific cables in tough Kevlar-type armor.
But sharks cause about one percent of damage. Ship anchors and fishing nets do far more.

description:
Sharks really have been reported biting undersea fiber cables, and Google armored its trans-Pacific cables partly because of it.
About 99 percent of international internet traffic runs through seabed cables, but sharks caused only about 1 percent of deep-sea damage; most faults come from fishing and shipping.
Had you ever wondered how the internet crosses the ocean? Comment below.
first_comment: Roughly 70 percent of cable faults trace back to fishing and shipping, according to the International Cable Protection Committee. Did you think satellites carried your internet?
